sanskrit: ajñātaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya yatnena mahatā tataḥ sodaraṃ pātayām āsa gāndhārī duḥkhamūrcchitā
english: Unknown to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with great effort and then faint with grief, Gāndhārī caused her own foetus — her very womb-child — to miscarry.

sanskrit: tato jajñe māṃsapeśī lohāṣṭhīleva saṃhatā dvivarṣasaṃbhṛtāṃ kukṣau tām utsraṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Then there issued forth a mass of flesh, hard as an iron ball, that had been carried in the womb for two full years; she set about expelling it.

sanskrit: atha dvaipāyano jñātvā tvaritaḥ samupāgamat tāṃ sa māṃsamayīṃ peśīṃ dadarśa japatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Dvaipāyana, having learned of this by his insight, came swiftly; that best of murmurers of mantras beheld the fleshy mass.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt saubaleyīṃ kim idaṃ te cikīrṣitam sā cātmano mataṃ satyaṃ śaśaṃsa paramarṣaye
english: Then he said to the daughter of Subala: 'What is it you intend to do?' And she truthfully disclosed her own intention to that supreme seer.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaṃ kuntīsutaṃ jātaṃ śrutvā ravisamaprabham duḥkhena parameṇedam udaraṃ pātitaṃ mayā
english: 'Having heard that Kuntī's eldest son was born, radiant as the sun, I caused this womb to be expelled by me out of extreme grief.'

sanskrit: śataṃ ca kila putrāṇāṃ vitīrṇaṃ me tvayā purā iyaṃ ca me māṃsapeśī jātā putraśatāya vai
english: 'And indeed a hundred sons were granted to me by you before; yet this mass of flesh has been born — truly, as the gift of a hundred sons.'

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evam etat saubaleyi naitaj jātv anyathā bhavet vitathaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā
english: Vyāsa said: 'So it shall be, O daughter of Subala — this can never be otherwise. I have never spoken falsely, not even in jest; how then could it be otherwise?'

sanskrit: ghṛtapūrṇaṃ kuṇḍaśataṃ kṣipram eva vidhīyatām śītābhir adbhir aṣṭhīlām imāṃ ca pariṣiñcata
english: 'Let a hundred pots filled with clarified butter be prepared at once, and sprinkle this solid lump with cold water.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā sicyamānā aṣṭhīlā abhavac chatadhā tadā aṅguṣṭhaparvamātrāṇāṃ garbhāṇāṃ pṛthag eva tu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As that solid lump was being sprinkled, it split into a hundred portions at once — each being a separate embryo of the size of a thumb-joint.

sanskrit: ekādhikaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ yathāyogaṃ viśāṃ pate māṃsapeśyās tadā rājan kramaśaḥ kālaparyayāt
english: One hundred and one in full number, O lord of the people — thus, O king, from that mass of flesh, each appeared in due order as time passed.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃs teṣu kuṇḍeṣu garbhān avadadhe tadā svanugupteṣu deśeṣu rakṣāṃ ca vyadadhāt tataḥ
english: Then he placed those embryos each in its own pot, in well-guarded places, and thereafter arranged their protection.

sanskrit: śaśāsa caiva bhagavān kālenaitāvatā punaḥ vighaṭṭanīyāny etāni kuṇḍānīti sma saubalīm
english: And the blessed one also instructed the daughter of Subala: 'These pots are to be opened again only after this much time has elapsed.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā bhagavān vyāsas tathā pratividhāya ca jagāma tapase dhīmān himavantaṃ śiloccayam
english: Having said this and having made all the arrangements, the blessed and wise Vyāsa departed for austerities to the Himālaya, that mountain of rocks.

sanskrit: jajñe krameṇa caitena teṣāṃ duryodhano nṛpaḥ janmatas tu pramāṇena jyeṣṭho rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Through this process, Duryodhana came to be born as the king among them; yet by birth reckoning, the elder king is Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: jātamātre sute tasmin dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam samānīya bahūn viprān bhīṣmaṃ viduram eva ca
english: The very moment that son was born, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having summoned many Brāhmaṇas and also Bhīṣma and Vidura, spoke thus.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro rājaputro jyeṣṭho naḥ kulavardhanaḥ prāptaḥ svaguṇato rājyaṃ na tasmin vācyam asti naḥ
english: 'Yudhiṣṭhira, the elder prince and increaser of our lineage, has attained the kingdom by his own merit — we have nothing to say against him.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tv anantaras tasmād api rājā bhaviṣyati etad dhi brūta me satyaṃ yad atra bhavitā dhruvam
english: 'But will this one, next after him, also become king? Tell me truly what shall certainly come to pass in this matter.'

sanskrit: vākyasyaitasya nidhane dikṣu sarvāsu bhārata kravyādāḥ prāṇadan ghorāḥ śivāś cāśivaśaṃsinaḥ
english: At the end of these words, O Bhārata, in all directions terrifying flesh-eating creatures cried out, and jackals howled their ill omens.

sanskrit: lakṣayitvā nimittāni tāni ghorāṇi sarvaśaḥ te 'bruvan brāhmaṇā rājan viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ
english: Having observed those dreadful portents on every side, O king, the Brāhmaṇas spoke, as did the great-minded Vidura.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ kulāntakaraṇo bhavitaiṣa sutas tava tasya śāntiḥ parityāge puṣṭyā tv apanayo mahān
english: 'Clearly this son of yours shall be the destroyer of the lineage. Peace lies in his abandonment; to keep him thriving is a great wrong.'

sanskrit: śatam ekonam apy astu putrāṇāṃ te mahīpate ekena kuru vai kṣemaṃ lokasya ca kulasya ca
english: 'Let your sons number one fewer than a hundred, O lord of the earth — secure the welfare of the world and of the lineage through that one act.'

sanskrit: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet
english: 'One should abandon one person for the sake of the family; abandon a family for the sake of a village; abandon a village for the sake of a kingdom; abandon the earth for the sake of the Self.'

sanskrit: sa tathā vidureṇoktas taiś ca sarvair dvijottamaiḥ na cakāra tathā rājā putrasnehasamanvitaḥ
english: Though thus advised by Vidura and by all those foremost twice-born, the king did not act accordingly, overcome as he was by affection for his son.

sanskrit: tataḥ putraśataṃ sarvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya pārthiva māsamātreṇa saṃjajñe kanyā caikā śatādhikā
english: Then all one hundred sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O king, were born within the space of a single month, and one daughter in addition to the hundred.

sanskrit: gāndhāryāṃ kliśyamānāyām udareṇa vivardhatā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahābāhuṃ vaiśyā paryacarat kila
english: While Gāndhārī was afflicted by her ever-growing womb, a Vaiśyā woman it is said attended upon the mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tasmin saṃvatsare rājan dhṛtarāṣṭrān mahāyaśāḥ jajñe dhīmāṃs tatas tasyāṃ yuyutsuḥ karaṇo nṛpa
english: In that same year, O king, the greatly renowned and wise Yuyutsu — a Kāraṇa — was born from her by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: evaṃ putraśataṃ jajñe dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ mahārathānāṃ vīrāṇāṃ kanyā caikātha duḥśalā
english: Thus were born the hundred sons of the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra — all mighty warriors and heroes — and one daughter, Duḥśalā.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca jyeṣṭhānujyeṣṭhatāṃ teṣāṃ nāmadheyāni cābhibho dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāṇām ānupūrvyeṇa kīrtaya
english: Janamejaya said: 'O master, recite in order the names and the seniority — eldest to youngest — of those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca duryodhano yuyutsuś ca rājan duḥśāsanas tathā duḥsaho duḥśalaś caiva jalasaṃdhaḥ samaḥ sahaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: 'Duryodhana, Yuyutsu, and also Duḥśāsana, O king; Duḥsaha, Duḥśalā, Jalasaṃdha, Sama, and Saha —

sanskrit: vindānuvindau durdharṣaḥ subāhur duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ durmarṣaṇo durmukhaś ca duṣkarṇaḥ karṇa eva ca
english: Vinda and Anuvinda, Durdharṣa, Subāhu, Duṣpradharṣaṇa, Durmarṣaṇa, Durmukha, Duṣkarṇa, and also Karṇa —

sanskrit: viviṃśatir vikarṇaś ca jalasaṃdhaḥ sulocanaḥ citropacitrau citrākṣaś cārucitraḥ śarāsanaḥ
english: Viviṃśati, Vikarṇa, Jalasaṃdha, Sulocana, Citra and Upacitra, Citrākṣa, Ārucitra, and Śarāsana —

sanskrit: durmado duṣpragāhaś ca vivitsur vikaṭaḥ samaḥ ūrṇanābhaḥ sunābhaś ca tathā nandopanandakau
english: Durmada, Duṣpragāha, Vivityu, Vikaṭa, Sama, Ūrṇanābha, Sunābha, and likewise Nanda and Upanandaka —

sanskrit: senāpatiḥ suṣeṇaś ca kuṇḍodaramahodarau citrabāṇaś citravarmā suvarmā durvimocanaḥ
english: Senāpati, Suṣeṇa, Kuṇḍodara, Mahodara, Citrabāṇa, Citravarmā, Suvarmā, and Durvimocana —

sanskrit: ayobāhur mahābāhuś citrāṅgaś citrakuṇḍalaḥ bhīmavego bhīmabalo balākī balavardhanaḥ
english: Ayobāhu, Mahābāhu, Citrāṅga, Citrakuṇḍala, Bhīmavega, Bhīmabala, Balākī, and Balavardhana —

sanskrit: ugrāyudho bhīmakarmā kanakāyur dṛḍhāyudhaḥ dṛḍhavarmā dṛḍhakṣatraḥ somakīrtir anūdaraḥ
english: Ugrāyudha, Bhīmakarman, Kanakāyu, Dṛḍhāyudha, Dṛḍhavarmā, Dṛḍhakṣatra, Somakīrti, and Anūdara —

sanskrit: dṛḍhasaṃdho jarāsaṃdhaḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ sadaḥsuvāk ugraśravā aśvasenaḥ senānīr duṣparājayaḥ
english: Dṛḍhasaṃdha, Jarāsaṃdha, Satyasaṃdha, Sadaḥsuvāk, Ugraśravā, Aśvasena, Senānī, and Duṣparājaya —

sanskrit: aparājitaḥ paṇḍitako viśālākṣo durāvaraḥ dṛḍhahastaḥ suhastaś ca vātavegasuvarcasau
english: Aparājita, Paṇḍitaka, Viśālākṣa, Durāvara, Dṛḍhahasta, Suhasta, and the pair Vātavega and Suvarcas —

sanskrit: ādityaketur bahvāśī nāgadantograyāyinau kavacī niṣaṅgī pāśī ca daṇḍadhāro dhanurgrahaḥ
english: Ādityaketu, Bahvāśī, Nāgadanta and Ugrayāyin, Kavacī, Niṣaṅgī, Pāśī, Daṇḍadhāra, and Dhanurgraha —

sanskrit: ugro bhīmaratho vīro vīrabāhur alolupaḥ abhayo raudrakarmā ca tathā dṛḍharathas trayaḥ
english: Ugra, Bhīmaratha, Vīra, Vīrabāhu, Alolupa, Abhaya, Raudrakarman, and likewise three others including Dṛḍharatha —

sanskrit: anādhṛṣyaḥ kuṇḍabhedī virāvī dīrghalocanaḥ dīrghabāhur mahābāhur vyūḍhoruḥ kanakadhvajaḥ
english: Anādhṛṣya, Kuṇḍabhedī, Virāvī, Dīrghalocana, Dīrghabāhu, Mahābāhu, Vyūḍhoru, and Kanakadhvaja —

sanskrit: kuṇḍāśī virajāś caiva duḥśalā ca śatādhikā etad ekaśataṃ rājan kanyā caikā prakīrtitā
english: Kuṇḍāśī and Virajā — and Duḥśalā as the one beyond the hundred. This is the full one hundred and one, O king, with one daughter named as well.'

sanskrit: nāmadheyānupūrvyeṇa viddhi janmakramaṃ nṛpa sarve tv atirathāḥ śūrāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english: 'Know the order of birth by the sequence of names, O king. All were atiratha warriors, all heroes, all skilled in battle.

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaś caiva rājaśāstreṣu kovidāḥ sarve saṃsargavidyāsu vidyābhijanaśobhinaḥ
english: All were knowers of the Vedas and versed in the science of kingship; all excelled in the arts of association, adorned by learning and noble birth.

sanskrit: sarveṣām anurūpāś ca kṛtā dārā mahīpate dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa samaye samīkṣya vidhivat tadā
english: Wives befitting every one of them were secured, O lord of the earth, by Dhṛtarāṣṭra in due season, having considered carefully and according to proper rites.

sanskrit: duḥśalāṃ samaye rājā sindhurājāya bhārata jayadrathāya pradadau saubalānumate tadā
english: At the proper time, O Bhārata, the king gave Duḥśalā to the king of Sindhu, Jayadratha, with the consent of the Subala line.'

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathito dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām ārṣaḥ saṃbhava uttamaḥ amānuṣo mānuṣāṇāṃ bhavatā brahmavittama
english: Janamejaya said: 'The supernal and extraordinary origin of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — transcending the human even among humans — has been narrated by you, O best of those who know Brahman.

sanskrit: nāmadheyāni cāpy eṣāṃ kathyamānāni bhāgaśaḥ tvattaḥ śrutāni me brahman pāṇḍavānāṃ tu kīrtaya
english: 'Their names too, spoken portion by portion, have been heard by me from you, O Brāhmaṇa. Now recite the birth of the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: te hi sarve mahātmāno devarājaparākramāḥ tvayaivāṃśāvataraṇe devabhāgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
english: 'For all of them are great-souled, with the valour of the king of the gods; they themselves were declared by you to be divine portions descended in the chapter on the descent of the divine shares.'

sanskrit: tasmād icchāmy ahaṃ śrotum atimānuṣakarmaṇām teṣām ājananaṃ sarvaṃ vaiśaṃpāyana kīrtaya
english: 'Therefore I wish to hear all about the origin of those whose deeds surpass the human. Recite it fully, O Vaiśaṃpāyana.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājā pāṇḍur mahāraṇye mṛgavyālaniṣevite vane maithunakālasthaṃ dadarśa mṛgayūthapam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: King Pāṇḍu, in a great forest frequented by deer and serpents, came upon the leader of a deer herd at the time of its mating.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ ca mṛgīṃ taṃ ca rukmapuṅkhaiḥ supatribhiḥ nirbibheda śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ pāṇḍuḥ pañcabhir āśugaiḥ
english: Then Pāṇḍu pierced both the doe and that stag with five swift, sharp arrows feathered with gold-tipped shafts.

sanskrit: sa ca rājan mahātejā ṛṣiputras tapodhanaḥ bhāryayā saha tejasvī mṛgarūpeṇa saṃgataḥ
english: And that one, O king, was in truth a great-spirited son of a seer, rich in austerity, a radiant being who had joined with his wife in the form of a deer.

sanskrit: saṃsaktas tu tayā mṛgyā mānuṣīm īrayan giram kṣaṇena patito bhūmau vilalāpākulendriyaḥ
english: While still locked together with that doe, uttering human speech, he fell to the ground in an instant and lamented, his senses distraught.

sanskrit: mṛga uvāca kāmamanyuparītāpi buddhyaṅgarahitāpi ca varjayanti nṛśaṃsāni pāpeṣv abhiratā narāḥ
english: The deer said: 'Even men overcome by desire and anger, even those bereft of the limb of reason, even those addicted to sin — they shun acts of cruelty.

sanskrit: na vidhiṃ grasate prajñā prajñāṃ tu grasate vidhiḥ vidhiparyāgatān arthān prajñā na pratipadyate
english: 'Wisdom does not swallow fate, but fate swallows wisdom; wisdom does not comprehend those ends that have been overturned by fate.

sanskrit: śaśvaddharmātmanāṃ mukhye kule jātasya bhārata kāmalobhābhibhūtasya kathaṃ te calitā matiḥ
english: 'Born in the foremost lineage of those ever devoted to righteousness, O Bhārata — how has your mind been swayed, overpowered by desire and greed?'

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca śatrūṇāṃ yā vadhe vṛttiḥ sā mṛgāṇāṃ vadhe smṛtā rājñāṃ mṛga na māṃ mohāt tvaṃ garhayitum arhasi
english: Pāṇḍu said: 'The same conduct that applies to the slaying of enemies is held to apply to the slaying of deer for kings, O deer — you ought not, out of confusion, reproach me.'

sanskrit: acchadmanāmāyayā ca mṛgāṇāṃ vadha iṣyate sa eva dharmo rājñāṃ tu tad vidvān kiṃ nu garhase
english: 'The slaying of deer without disguise and without deceit is indeed desired; that very conduct is the duty of kings — knowing this, why do you reproach me?'

sanskrit: agastyaḥ satram āsīnaś cacāra mṛgayām ṛṣiḥ āraṇyān sarvadaivatyān mṛgān prokṣya mahāvane
english: 'The sage Agastya, while seated at a sacrifice, went out to hunt; having consecrated all the forest-dwelling, divinity-dwelling deer in the great forest —

sanskrit: pramāṇadṛṣṭadharmeṇa katham asmān vigarhase agastyasyābhicāreṇa yuṣmākaṃ vai vapā hutā
english: '— according to the dharma seen in scripture, how do you reproach us? Through the oblation-rite of Agastya, your very fat was indeed offered as an oblation.'

sanskrit: mṛga uvāca na ripūn vai samuddiśya vimuñcanti purā śarān randhra eṣāṃ viśeṣeṇa vadhakālaḥ praśasyate
english: The deer said: 'Formerly arrows were not released aiming at enemies in the midst of this act — indeed it is the finding of their vulnerable moment that is especially praised as the time of slaying.

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca pramattam apramattaṃ vā vivṛtaṃ ghnanti caujasā upāyair iṣubhis tīkṣṇaiḥ kasmān mṛga vigarhase
english: Pāṇḍu said: 'Whether heedless or heedful, whether exposed or concealed — kings slay powerfully, by stratagems and with sharp arrows. Why then do you reproach me, O deer?'

sanskrit: mṛga uvāca nāhaṃ ghnantaṃ mṛgān rājan vigarhe ātmakāraṇāt maithunaṃ tu pratīkṣyaṃ me syāt tvayehānṛśaṃsataḥ
english: The deer said: 'I do not reproach you for slaying deer, O king, on my own account — but the act of mating should have been awaited by you here, out of non-cruelty.'

sanskrit: sarvabhūtahite kāle sarvabhūtepsite tathā ko hi vidvān mṛgaṃ hanyāc carantaṃ maithunaṃ vane puruṣārthaphalaṃ kāntaṃ yat tvayā vitathaṃ kṛtam
english: 'At a time cherished and desired by all beings — what wise man would slay a deer engaged in mating in the forest? The dear fruit of the aims of man — that beloved thing you have made fruitless.'

sanskrit: pauravāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca teṣām akliṣṭakarmaṇām vaṃśe jātasya kauravya nānurūpam idaṃ tava
english: 'Born in the lineage of the Paurava kings and of those sages of effortless deeds, O Kauravya — this is not fitting for you.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaṃ karma sumahat sarvalokavigarhitam asvargyam ayaśasyaṃ ca adharmiṣṭhaṃ ca bhārata
english: 'This deed is exceedingly cruel, condemned by all the world, non-conducive to heaven, destructive to fame, and most unrighteous, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: strībhogānāṃ viśeṣajñaḥ śāstradharmārthatattvavit nārhas tvaṃ surasaṃkāśa kartum asvargyam īdṛśam
english: 'A connoisseur of the pleasures of women, a knower of the true nature of the dharma and artha of the scriptures — you who are like a god should not perform such a deed that shuts the door to heaven.'

sanskrit: tvayā nṛśaṃsakartāraḥ pāpācārāś ca mānavāḥ nigrāhyāḥ pārthivaśreṣṭha trivargaparivarjitāḥ
english: 'By you, O best of kings, those humans who commit cruelty and evil conduct, who are devoid of the three aims of life, ought to be suppressed — not emulated.'

sanskrit: kiṃ kṛtaṃ te naraśreṣṭha nighnato mām anāgasam muniṃ mūlaphalāhāraṃ mṛgaveṣadharaṃ nṛpa vasamānam araṇyeṣu nityaṃ śamaparāyaṇam
english: 'What have you done, O best of men, in slaying me, innocent as I am — a sage subsisting on roots and fruits, wearing the form of a deer, O king, ever dwelling in the forests, wholly devoted to tranquillity?'

sanskrit: tvayāhaṃ hiṃsito yasmāt tasmāt tvām apy asaṃśayam dvayor nṛśaṃsakartāram avaśaṃ kāmamohitam jīvitāntakaro bhāva evam evāgamiṣyati
english: 'Because you have injured me, therefore to you as well, without doubt — you who have acted cruelly toward both of us, who acted helplessly, deluded by desire — the end of life will come in this very same manner.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi kiṃdamo nāma tapasāpratimo muniḥ vyapatrapan manuṣyāṇāṃ mṛgyāṃ maithunam ācaram
english: 'For I am the sage Kiṃdama by name, without equal in austerity; being ashamed before humans, I was engaged in mating with my doe.'

sanskrit: mṛgo bhūtvā mṛgaiḥ sārdhaṃ carāmi gahane vane na tu te brahmahatyeyaṃ bhaviṣyaty avijānataḥ mṛgarūpadharaṃ hatvā mām evaṃ kāmamohitam
english: 'Having become a deer, I roam in the dense forest with other deer. Yet this shall not be a brahminicide for you, since you did not know you were slaying me who had taken the form of a deer, deluded thus by desire.'

sanskrit: asya tu tvaṃ phalaṃ mūḍha prāpsyasīdṛśam eva hi priyayā saha saṃvāsaṃ prāpya kāmavimohitaḥ tvam apy asyām avasthāyāṃ pretalokaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: 'But you, O fool, shall reap a fruit exactly like this — when you, deluded by desire, are together with your beloved wife, you too in that very condition shall pass to the realm of the dead.'

sanskrit: antakāle ca saṃvāsaṃ yayā gantāsi kāntayā pretarājavaśaṃ prāptaṃ sarvabhūtaduratyayam bhaktyā matimatāṃ śreṣṭha saiva tvām anuyāsyati
english: 'And the beloved one with whom you shall pass to the realm of Yama, king of the dead — that realm irresistible to all beings — she, out of devotion, O best of the wise, shall follow you there.'

sanskrit: vartamānaḥ sukhe duḥkhaṃ yathāhaṃ prāpitas tvayā tathā sukhaṃ tvāṃ saṃprāptaṃ duḥkham abhyāgamiṣyati
english: 'Just as I, in the midst of happiness, have been brought to grief by you — so grief shall come upon you when happiness has arrived.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā suduḥkhārto jīvitāt sa vyayujyata mṛgaḥ pāṇḍuś ca śokārtaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, afflicted with the greatest pain, that deer was parted from life; and Pāṇḍu too was struck with grief in an instant.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ vyatītam atikramya rājā svam iva bāndhavam sabhāryaḥ śokaduḥkhārtaḥ paryadevayad āturaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The king, having stepped past that one who had passed away as though it were his own kinsman, together with his wife, afflicted with sorrow and grief, lamented in anguish.

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca satām api kule jātāḥ karmaṇā bata durgatim prāpnuvanty akṛtātmānaḥ kāmajālavimohitāḥ
english: Pāṇḍu said: 'Alas — even those born in noble lineages reach misfortune through their deeds, those who have not mastered the self, deluded by the snare of desire.

sanskrit: śaśvad dharmātmanā jāto bāla eva pitā mama jīvitāntam anuprāptaḥ kāmātmaiveti naḥ śrutam
english: 'My father, though born of one ever devoted to righteousness, even as a young man met his end — enslaved by desire, so we have heard.

sanskrit: tasya kāmātmanaḥ kṣetre rājñaḥ saṃyatavāg ṛṣiḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ sākṣād bhagavān mām ajījanat
english: 'In the field of that desire-enslaved king, the sage Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana — the blessed one himself, restrained of speech — begot me directly.'
